Aims to cut GETBLOCKTXN round trips and speed up block propagation without any protocol change
Benefits every node and the wider network by lowering stale-block races

result.summary: This PR adds prefilling of CMPCTBLOCK announcements: instead of only prefilling the coinbase, the node also includes transactions it believes a peer will be missing, based on what it itself needed via GETBLOCKTXN or its extra pool during the last reconstruction. It limits how much it prefills based on the peer's live TCP window so it avoids forcing an extra round trip at the transport layer. To do this it adds cross-platform TCP_INFO / send-queue introspection helpers to util/sock and net, plus bookkeeping in blockencodings.cpp to track prefill candidates and their sizes.
result.problem: Compact block reconstruction still frequently requires a GETBLOCKTXN round trip when a peer is missing transactions, slowing block propagation across the network and increasing stale rates, which affects miners and full nodes broadly (author measured 56.9% reconstruction-without-roundtrip today vs 89.7% with TCP-window-limited prefilling).

categories.name: p2p
categories.evidence: Directly changes compact block relay (blockencodings.cpp/h), net_processing.cpp, and net.cpp/h to implement CMPCTBLOCK prefilling and TCP-window-aware send logic; carries the P2P label.
categories.rationale: Improves compact block reconstruction rates from a measured 56.9% to 89.7% without a protocol change, per the author's data, which reduces propagation delay network-wide; backward compatible with unmodified peers. Not P1 because it is an enhancement rather than a fix for a correctness, security, or DoS problem, and delay in merging does not break anything currently working.

categories.name: build
categories.evidence: CMakeLists.txt is touched to bump the minimum targeted Windows version so SIO_TCP_INFO is available at build time.
categories.rationale: A one-line minimum-Windows-version bump needed only to unlock a Windows API used elsewhere in this PR; the commit message says 'this is needed for the use of the SIO_TCP_INFO API'. Narrow, mechanical, and only relevant as a dependency of the p2p feature.

categories.name: tests
categories.evidence: The test/bench/fuzz changes (blockencodings_tests, cmpctblock fuzz target, sock_tests, bench/blockencodings) all pin the behavior of specific areas (compact block encoding, socket TCP info) rather than changing shared test framework or infrastructure.
categories.rationale: Per the tests category definition, tests that pin one area's behavior belong to that area, not to test infrastructure; these tests are all specific to the p2p compact-block and utils socket changes in this PR.

categories.name: utils
categories.evidence: Adds substantial new cross-platform socket introspection code to src/util/sock.cpp/h: a TCPInfo wrapper, GetTCPWindowSize, and GetOSBytesQueued covering Linux, BSDs, macOS, and Windows.
categories.rationale: A new, genuinely reusable low-level primitive for reading TCP window/queue state across five platform variants; correctness matters since subtle platform-specific bugs are easy to introduce here, and reviewers already found and fixed a use-after-free in adjacent counting logic. It is driven entirely by the p2p prefill feature rather than a standing utils need, keeping it below P2.

uncertainties: Whether #35724 is a strict dependency or just a sibling refactor the author chose to rebase onto; the stack facts show no formal based_on relationship despite the description implying one
Whether the m4ycon-reported prefilled_size==0 logging bug is now fully resolved after the 2026-08-04 rebase, since the discussion ends shortly after that push without explicit confirmation
How to weigh the util/sock.cpp TCPInfo code: it is large and platform-spanning but entirely motivated by this single p2p feature, so its 'utils' importance is somewhat borrowed rather than intrinsic
result.card: This PR adds prefilling of CMPCTBLOCK announcements with transactions a peer is predicted to need, limited by the peer's live TCP window so prefilling never forces an extra round trip, aiming to reduce GETBLOCKTXN round trips and speed block propagation. The author's own measurements show reconstruction-without-roundtrip rising from 56.9% (coinbase-only prefill) to 89.7% with window-limited prefilling, a meaningful and backward-compatible improvement felt by the whole p2p network. Seven members gave concept ACKs and two contributors ran it and gave tested ACKs with data; reviewers (andrewtoth, m4ycon) found and got fixed real bugs including a use-after-free and miscounted stats, with no standing objection to the approach. It touches p2p (net_processing, net, blockencodings) as its core, adds a reusable cross-platform TCP-info primitive to util/sock, and needs a one-line Windows minimum-version bump in the build system. It has been rebased onto sibling PR #35724, which split out logging commits, and the author asks reviewers to look at #35724 first.
